title: Pulled quotient generator equations and descent through K-flat resolutions
statement:
Let $g:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes. Use the Noetherian adic datum $A,I,P_n=A/I^n$ ($n\geq1$), small pro-etale sites and coefficient sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For $W=T,T'$ put $B_W=A_W=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_W$, $R_W=\underline A_W$ and $S_{n,W}=(P_n)_W$, with quotient ring maps $q_{b,a}$ for $b\geq a\geq1$. Use module pullbacks $g_R^*,g_n^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], exact scalar restriction $\operatorname{Res}$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and unbounded module-sheaf derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $P$ be any flat-term K-flat $B_T$-complex [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Set $P_n=P\otimes_{B_T}S_{n,T}$, $U=g_R^*\operatorname{Res}P$, $Z_n=U\otimes_{R_{T'}}S_{n,T'}$, and $V_n=g_n^*P_n$. Let $t_n:Z_n\to V_n$, $h_{b,a}:V_b\otimes_{S_{b,T'}}S_{a,T'}\to V_a$ and $n_{b,a}:Z_b\otimes_{S_{b,T'}}S_{a,T'}\to Z_a$ be the specified actual sheaf tensor maps of [lem-weil-pbc-pulled-reduction-flat-model-formulas]. Thus $e_n(x)=[x\otimes1]$, $\bar r_n$ is the image of $r\in R_{T'}$ in $S_{n,T'}$, and $t_n$ sends $([x]\otimes r)\otimes t$ to $e_n(x)\bar r_n t$. Use the actual pure tensors of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus] and scalar associators of [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization].

The composites $h_{b,a}(t_b\otimes1)$ and $t_a n_{b,a}$ are equal as morphisms of sheaf tensor complexes. On $(([x]\otimes r)\otimes t)\otimes s$ their respective values are
$$e_a(x)q_{b,a}(\bar r_b t)s=e_a(x)\bar r_a q_{b,a}(t)s.$$
Here the coefficient identities are $q_{b,a}(\bar r_b)=\bar r_a$ and $q_{b,a}(rs)=q_{b,a}(r)q_{b,a}(s)$ for local $S_{b,T'}$-sections $r,s$; the equality of tensor maps is on the whole sheafified complexes, not only on pure tensors before sheafification.

For $c\geq b\geq a\geq1$, on $((e_c(x)t)\otimes s)\otimes v$ the composite through $b$ has the successive values
$$(e_b(x)q_{c,b}(t)s)\otimes v\longmapsto e_a(x)q_{b,a}(q_{c,b}(t)s)v=e_a(x)q_{c,a}(t)q_{b,a}(s)v.$$
The direct $h_{c,a}$ composite after canonical scalar reassociation has the same last value. This is an equality of sheaf tensor complex maps, with $q_{b,a}q_{c,b}=q_{c,a}$. Before inverse image the two corresponding composites both send $((x\otimes t)\otimes s)\otimes v$ to $x\otimes q_{c,a}(t)q_{b,a}(s)v$. For equal indices $h_{a,a}$ is precisely $h\otimes s\mapsto hs$, inverse $h\mapsto h\otimes1$; the corresponding maps before inverse image and for $n_{a,a}$ are their scalar unit identifications.

These formulas are natural for every chain map $f:P\to P'$: on every generator the induced maps replace $x$ by $f(x)$. They commute with the tensor differentials of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], with coefficients placed in degree zero. Under the canonical K-flat representative comparisons for derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and derived ringed pullback [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback], they induce natural transformations on all of $D(B_T)$. Scalar extension sends quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat models to quasi-isomorphisms and has canonical comparisons between any two resolutions, composable for a third resolution. Separately, pullback sends quasi-isomorphisms between flat-term K-flat models to quasi-isomorphisms and its resolution comparisons are canonical and composable. Under the equivalence $W_{B_T}^{-1}\mathcal P_{B_T}\simeq D(B_T)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], where $\mathcal P_{B_T}$ is the full homotopy subcategory of flat-term K-flat complexes and $W_{B_T}$ its quasi-isomorphisms, the maps, their inverses, and the displayed square, triple and unit equalities all descend. The resulting derived transformations and equalities are independent of the chosen $P$ for every $K\in D(B_T)$, with no completeness hypothesis. In particular, if $\tau_n,\theta^H_{b,a},\theta^N_{b,a}$ denote their canonically identified localizations in the finite coefficient derived categories, then
$$\theta^H_{b,a}\circ(\tau_b\otimes^L1)=\tau_a\circ\theta^N_{b,a},$$
and the stated triple and unit identities hold for these very derived maps.

proof.text: Fix the flat-term K-flat complex $P$. The flat-model-formulas node supplies the actual balanced sheaf-complex isomorphisms $t_n,h_{b,a},n_{b,a}$, their inverses, and the K-flat flat-term status of all their sources and targets, including successive quotient tensors. Thus none of the following calculations assumes that $S_b\to S_a$ is flat. We use the section calculus degreewise: linear maps out of each sheaf tensor are determined by pure sections; for iterated tensors apply this determination successively to the factors. All maps used below are already maps of sheaves, so equality on these local generators proves equality after sheafification as well.

proof.text: On $(([x]\otimes r)\otimes t)\otimes s$, first $t_b\otimes1$ and then $h_{b,a}$ give $e_a(x)q_{b,a}(\bar r_b t)s$. First $n_{b,a}$ and then $t_a$ give $e_a(x)\bar r_a q_{b,a}(t)s$. A quotient ring map preserves multiplication, and the images of $r$ in the quotient sheaves satisfy $q_{b,a}(\bar r_b)=\bar r_a$ by their definition as the compatible coefficient maps. Hence the outputs agree. The determination in step 1 proves the square equality as sheaf-complex morphisms.

source.place: Paragraphs 1–2, compatibility with transition maps and normalization cocycles; explicit agent calculation using the stated flat-model formulas.

proof.text: For $c\geq b\geq a$, applying $h_{c,b}\otimes1$ and $h_{b,a}$ to $((e_c(x)t)\otimes s)\otimes v$ gives successively $(e_b(x)q_{c,b}(t)s)\otimes v$ and $e_a(x)q_{b,a}(q_{c,b}(t)s)v=e_a(x)q_{c,a}(t)q_{b,a}(s)v$. Scalar reassociation first gives $(e_c(x)t)\otimes q_{b,a}(s)v$, and $h_{c,a}$ gives this same final output. Here multiplicativity and $q_{b,a}q_{c,b}=q_{c,a}$ are the quotient identities in the datum. Before inverse image the identical computation replaces $e_j(x)$ by $x\otimes1$, yielding $x\otimes q_{c,a}(t)q_{b,a}(s)v$. For the $n$ maps replace $e_j(x)t$ by $u\otimes t$; the common output is $u\otimes q_{c,a}(t)q_{b,a}(s)v$. Repeated pure-section determination proves these equalities on the sheaves, with the scalar associators specified in the normalization node.

proof.text: At equal indices $q_{a,a}=1$. Thus $h_{a,a}$ sends $(e_a(x)t)\otimes s$ to $e_a(x)ts$, so it is scalar multiplication. Its inverse sends $h$ to $h\otimes1$: the two composites are identities because $(hs)\otimes1=h\otimes s$ is the balancing relation. Before inverse image the formula is $(x\otimes t)\otimes s\mapsto x\otimes ts$; for $n_{a,a}$ it is $(u\otimes t)\otimes s\mapsto u\otimes ts$. These are the scalar unit identifications, with the same inverses. Their equalities are sheaf equalities by the section calculus.

proof.text: For a chain map $f:P\to P'$, either order of $f$ and each displayed comparison replaces $x$ by $f(x)$ and leaves every coefficient unchanged. This proves naturality by pure-section determination. In degree $i$ the differential of a tensor with these degree-zero coefficient complexes is $d_P\otimes1$. For example both differential composites for $t_n$ send $([x]\otimes r)\otimes t$ to $e_n(d_Px)\bar r_n t$; for $h$ and $n$ the same substitution in their formulas proves the chain equations. The inverse formulas satisfy them too. The termwise additive functors also preserve chain homotopies: apply the functor degreewise to $f-f'=dH+Hd$; additivity and preservation of composition give the same equation. Thus the functors and these natural isomorphisms are defined on the full homotopy subcategory $\mathcal P_{B_T}$.

proof.text: Compose these model functors with derived localization in their target coefficient categories. They invert $W_{B_T}$. Indeed restriction to $R_T$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms because its underlying abelian sheaves are unchanged, and the flat-model node puts the restrictions in the K-flat flat-term class. Derived change of rings preserves quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes, separately at $B_T\to S_{n,T}$, $R_{T'}\to S_{n,T'}$ and $S_{b,T'}\to S_{a,T'}$. Ringed-topos derived pullback preserves quasi-isomorphisms between flat-term K-flat models, separately for $g_R^*$ and $g_n^*$. The flat-model node verifies the required class at every intermediate output and identifies the resulting localized functors with $N_n,H_n$ and their successive derived scalar extensions. The change-of-rings node gives canonical resolution comparisons compatible with a third resolution; the ringed-pullback node gives the corresponding assertion separately for pullback.

proof.text: The site-derived-tensor-descent node identifies $W_{B_T}^{-1}\mathcal P_{B_T}$ with $D(B_T)$. Apply the localization universal property to the functors of step 6 and to the natural transformations of step 5, with each fixed target $D(S_{a,T'})$. It gives unique descended transformations and preserves identities and composition; descending the inverse maps therefore gives their inverses. Since two transformations are equal if their restrictions to models agree, the square of step 2 and the triple and unit identities of steps 3–4 remain equalities after descent. The canonical model identifications in the flat-model node identify the descended $t_n,h_{b,a},n_{b,a}$ with the specified $\tau_n,\theta^H_{b,a},\theta^N_{b,a}$. Consequently $\theta^H_{b,a}\circ(\tau_b\otimes^L1)=\tau_a\circ\theta^N_{b,a}$ for these maps. Uniqueness of the lift makes the identification independent of any resolution and compatible with all third-resolution comparisons. Every $K\in D(B_T)$ has such a model by the flat-model node, without a completeness or boundedness assumption.

The delivery adds no new nodes; it is not superseded, since live and side-live both have the item unsplit; its statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to live; there is no cycle; proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. The item has no repair note of its own: the parent's re-split note is resolved, and that re-split created this item. Source checks: the main-20261015 completed-pullback-reduction statement claims compatibility with transition maps and normalization cocycles, and its proof only says these are inherited from the tower; the item writes this out, and proof_origin agent is correct. Stacks 0G7D (sites-cohomology.tex:3418), 0G7E and 06YY are the K-flat background. I recomputed every step. Step 2 (square): both sides equal e_a(x)q_{b,a}(r̄_b t)s = e_a(x)r̄_a q_{b,a}(t)s, by multiplicativity and q(r̄_b)=r̄_a. Step 3 (triple): both routes give e_a(x)q_{c,a}(t)q_{b,a}(s)v, using the associator of lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization on V_c, which is K-flat with flat terms; the variant before inverse image and the n variant also match. Step 4 (unit): q_{a,a}=1 makes the map multiplication, inverted by h↦h⊗1 through balancing. Step 5: naturality holds on generators, the differential is d_P⊗1 with no signs, and homotopies are preserved. Step 6: quasi-isomorphisms pass through Res, g_R^*, ⊗S_n, ⊗S_a and through ⊗S_n, g_n^*, using exactly the K-flat classes the flat-model node supplies. Step 7: P_{B_T}→D(B_T) is a localization (site-derived-tensor-descent, first clause only), so the Mathlib localization leaf gives unique lifts, inverses and equality on models, and the flat-model representation identifies the lifts with τ_n, θ^H and θ^N for every K. Edge cases checked: a=b=c, the zero complex, non-flat quotients such as Z/4→Z/2, and f=id. Accepted tool_uses: lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings and lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization, both generic coefficient calculus. A DAG search found no duplicate. No fixes.
